raw_response:
I will do it much like last year, because this wheat-maize rotation on 14 mu has to be steady, not fancy. Around here in Quzhou, if wheat is short of fertilizer, the ears stay small, and if maize is hungry after wheat harvest, it will lose yield fast, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the field go empty. I have well water, so I will use that advantage and not let the crop suffer dry spells. For wheat, I will put the main fertilizer in before sowing, use rotary tillage to mix it in, then topdress nitrogen at greening and jointing depending on how the stand looks. For maize, time is tight after wheat harvest, so I will keep it simple, use hybrid seed, mostly no-tillage or very light opening after the wheat, put fertilizer down early, and make sure I water at the key time. I do not chase too many new tricks. I look at what worked on my own land and what the neighbors got from fields like mine, then I keep the rates solid enough to protect yield and keep the cost within what a 2-person household can carry.
